analysis: detection power of dot-Identifiability-v1 by estimator class and structure

protocol.false_effect: |pred(do v) - pred(do a_ref)| >= 0.1, a_ref = x_obs[onset, A]

route.rule: tau = 0 (rule 3: A is not an ancestor of Y)

preregistered.statement: every naive effect-sign accuracy lies in [0.4, 0.6]

the best identification-aware estimator beats the best naive one (95% CI above 0) on back_door, confounder_mediator, instrumental_variable and front_door, and none applies on bi_variate, unobserved_confounder or bow_graph
the GraphRouter is not significantly worse (95% CI upper bound >= 0) than any other valid estimator on any structure
on unobserved_confounder the router's tau = 0 has a false-effect rate of exactly 0, while NaiveOLS and do-SVAR exceed 0.1

on bow_graph no identification-aware estimator applies, the router reports no identification, and NaiveOLS and do-SVAR lose effect-sign accuracy relative to bi_variate (95% CI of the difference above 0)

parts.check: NaiveOLS loses accuracy from bi_variate to bow_graph
do-SVAR loses accuracy from bi_variate to bow_graph

preregistered.statement: anticipated exception to P3: on mediator queried after the onset, the router (contemporaneous NaiveOLS) is significantly worse than do-SVAR, which models the lag
anticipated exception to P3: on confounder_mediator FrontDoorOLS scores at least as high as the routed BackDoorOLS (point estimates)

on observed_confounder the contemporaneous back-door set leaves A(t-1) paths open: BackDoorOLS (the router) makes false effects at a rate >= 0.1, below NaiveOLS, and do-SVAR, which conditions on the lags, makes fewer than BackDoorOLS
do-SVAR beats the best naive estimator (95% CI above 0) on bi_variate and, when it is queried after the onset, on mediator
the oracle scores 1 wherever the effect sign is defined and makes no false effect
